_note: Hand-maintained. Sign labels only, aggregate: no Linear A words. Each entry is one ending- or prefix-channel alternation the field has proposed by eye, or a source that was checked and yielded no specific pair. 'pair' is null when the source makes only a general claim (no specific sign-label pair to search for) or could not be read this session. Citations point to page images or cached text actually read for this spike (2026-09-12); see RESULT.md for how each was verified.

proposals.paraphrase: The ja-/a- alternation on (j)a-sa-sa-ra-me is 'attested in [a] securely connected context'.

proposals.citation: Facchetti 1999, p.132 n.73 (same word pair, read at the two-sign prefix split)
proposals.paraphrase: Same (j)a-sa-sa-ra-me alternation, one sign further in: a-sa- vs ja-sa-.
a-ta-i-jo-wa-ja and a-ta-i-jo-wa-e given as the same dedicant-name word, ending alternating.
u-na-ka-na-si and u-na-ru-ka-na-ti given as the same second-formula word, ending alternating (his own text also inserts -ru-, so the two forms are not identical apart from the ending).
Suffix -te/-ti glossed 'from/of', following Valerio; noted as one of the root i-*301's seven possible suffixes (-ti- and -e- listed separately, p.4).

proposals.citation: Thomas 2020, p.4 n.5, citing Steele and Meissner 2017:103
proposals.paraphrase: wa-/-u- suffix alternation illustrated by qe-ra2-u / qa-ra2-wa, said to recur elsewhere in Linear A (a different word pair from the one it illustrates, and differing at both ends, not one position).

proposals.citation: Duhoux 1978, in Etudes minoennes I, 65-129 (verification S: search-snippet only, not read in full)
proposals.paraphrase: General claim that the language of Linear A makes heavy use of prefixes and suffixes in word formation; no specific sign pair is available to us to check.

proposals.citation: Monti 2022, Kadmos 61:107-116 (verification P: seen restated, not read in full)
proposals.paraphrase: Reads a-/ja- as an article-like prefix on (j)a-sa-sa-ra-me, the same alternation Facchetti and Thomas discuss.

proposals.citation: Schoep 2002 - not in docs/works/; claims.md lists it only as an uncatalogued lead, on Hagia Triada place names
proposals.paraphrase: Not read. What is known of it (place-name study) is not a morphological ending/prefix claim, so there is nothing to search for.

proposals.citation: Davis 2013, Kadmos 52:35-52; Davis 2014, Aegaeum 36 (both catalogued in docs/works/)
proposals.paraphrase: Argues libation-formula word order (VSO) and catalogues stone vessels with vowel frequencies; neither page gives a specific ending or prefix sign-pair to search for.

proposals.citation: Younger, Linear A Texts & Inscriptions in phonetic transcription (site decommissioned 2024)
